# Compatibility and deprecation policy

Policy version: `1.0.0`. Status: **normative**. Effective date: **2026-08-02**.

This is the B10 compatibility authority for the CLI, public library, profile behavior, versioned
output schemas, diagnostic baselines, and standards knowledge packs. The machine-readable authority
is [`compatibility-policy.v1.json`](../../packages/core/policies/compatibility-policy.v1.json).
`validateCompatibilityPolicy` verifies an untrusted copy against the exact published authority, and
`classifyCompatibilityChange` fails closed for unknown surfaces or changes.

Both public functions are hostile-input boundaries and return deeply frozen results. Classification
accepts only bounded ASCII identifier segments: at most 64 bytes for a surface and 256 bytes for a
change. Rejections use stable non-reflective text, so control characters, bidirectional controls,
huge values, or secret-bearing input cannot be copied into logs by the classifier.

The policy applies to intentional changes and bug fixes whose observable result differs from the
published contract. Calling a change a correction does not make it compatible. If classification is
disputed, use the higher-risk class until the required owners agree. Notice and support windows are
minimums, not a promise that unsafe, compromised, revoked, or upstream-impossible behavior will
remain active.

## Release rules

- Stable public APIs start at major version 1. Patch releases preserve accepted inputs, outputs,
  documented behavior, and security posture. Backward-compatible additions and deprecations use
  minor releases. Incompatible changes use major releases.
- `@agent-context/core` and `@agent-context/lint` are versioned together until a superseding ADR and
  tested compatibility matrix say otherwise.
- The `1.0.0` release is stable. Any future pre-release line must publish separate release notes and
  migration fixtures before distribution.
- A published version is immutable. An accidental break is withdrawn or superseded, affected
  versions are documented, compatibility is restored promptly, and the artifact is never rewritten.
- A planned removal must satisfy both its day count and its minor-release count. The deprecated path
  remains functional and tested throughout that window. Removal then requires a major release.
- Previous-major support begins when the successor major reaches GA. During the stated period, high
  and critical security fixes are backported when technically safe; users receive an upgrade path
  and explicit end date. Immutable schemas, evidence snapshots, baselines, and pack identities
  remain addressable where their retention is `indefinite`.
- Maintenance support and artifact availability are separate. Support may end after the documented
  window, but every published public npm package version remains downloadable indefinitely. End of
  life uses npm deprecation, which preserves dependent builds, rather than project-initiated
  unpublishing.
- Availability can be lost only through a registry-enforced, legal, privacy, or security takedown
  outside project control: A registry-enforced, legal, privacy, or security takedown outside project
  control may make bytes unavailable; retain the immutable package name, version, digest, reason,
  and incident identity, and never reuse the identity.

| Surface               |   Notice | Deprecated minor releases | Previous-major support | Artifact retention |
| --------------------- | -------: | ------------------------: | ---------------------: | ------------------ |
| `cli`                 | 180 days |                         2 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |
| `public-library`      | 180 days |                         2 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |
| `profile-behavior`    |  90 days |                         1 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |
| `output-schema`       | 180 days |                         2 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |
| `diagnostic-baseline` | 180 days |                         2 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |
| `knowledge-pack`      |  30 days |                         1 |               365 days | `indefinite`       |

## Schema identity and migration

Every product schema declares its exact dialect and immutable `$id`; every instance carries the
family-specific `recordKind` and semantic `schemaVersion`. An identifier is never reassigned to a
changed shape or meaning. Minor additions are accepted only where old producers remain valid and
every supported consumer has documented unknown-field/value behavior. Closed older validators
continue to reject newer producers; a compatibility classification never bypasses exact runtime
validation.

A supported old version has an explicit schema/export, validator, frozen positive/negative/boundary
fixtures, and a pure migration. Migration validates the source, writes a separate destination
atomically, validates it completely, and preserves the original. Down-conversion is offered only
when reviewed as lossless or when documented loss is explicit. Persisted baselines and reports are
never edited in place.

## Profile drift and uncertainty

A changed vendor page, client release, or observation creates a review trigger and a new dated
`specSnapshotId`; it does not rewrite old evidence or prove runtime behavior. Profile changes record
source URL, retrieval date, client/upstream version, revision or digest, observed-versus-documented
differences, and assumptions. Undocumented, model-selected, UI-only, hosted, or version-dependent
behavior remains `conditional`, `unknown`, or `contradiction` until evidence supports a narrower
state.

If upstream removes behavior before the ordinary profile window can finish, the project retains the
historical snapshot, marks current support accurately, and uses the emergency record below if
retaining the old behavior is impossible or unsafe. It does not invent an alias, precedence rule, or
activation result to simulate compatibility.

## Baseline comparability

Diagnostic baselines compare only matching schema and fingerprint-method versions unless an explicit
migrator produces a separately validated baseline. A comparability-affecting change requires a
reviewed migration; no conversion can manufacture comparability.

## Knowledge-pack trust and rollback

H01 pack content versions are exact SemVer values bound to canonical RFC 8785 bytes, length, and
SHA-256 digest; bundled pack `schemaVersion`, `adapterVersion`, `rulesetVersion`, and
`minEngineVersion` are separate exact SemVer identities. Packs are data only. Discovery, parsing,
precedence, imports, glob semantics, executable rule logic, or trust behavior require an engine
release. H01 parsing alone never authorizes activation: H02 owns the exact TUF trust design and H03
must verify metadata, target path/length/digest, channel, schema version, and minimum engine before
parsing. Stable and preview remain separate delegated roles.

The same version with different bytes, expired or inconsistent metadata,
rollback/freeze/mix-and-match evidence, wrong channel, unsupported engine, revoked target, or
unknown root fails closed. CI never silently updates. Rollback restores only a previously verified,
compatible, non-revoked lock. A yank stops new selection without rewriting history; a security
revocation blocks activation but retains the digest and incident identity for audit. Registry outage
leaves verified locked offline scanning available and reports freshness as unknown rather than
claiming global currency.

## Emergency security exception

Only these triggers may shorten notice:

- `active-p0-security-incident`: active p0 security incident.

- `compromised-release-signing-or-standards-trust-infrastructure`: compromised release signing or
  standards trust infrastructure.

- `urgent-rollback-of-harmful-published-artifact`: urgent rollback of harmful published artifact.

- `forced-upstream-removal-that-makes-retained-behavior-unsafe-or-impossible`: forced upstream
  removal that makes retained behavior unsafe or impossible.

Break-glass access expires within 4 hours. It requires `security-reviewers`,
`governance-reviewers-or-release-managers`, `affected-domain-owner`, review within 24 hours, and a
retrospective within 5 business days. The record must contain:

- `incident-id-trigger-and-affected-versions`: incident id trigger and affected versions.

- `dri-independent-approvers-and-utc-timeline`: dri independent approvers and utc timeline.

- `compatibility-impact-and-shortened-window-rationale`: compatibility impact and shortened window
  rationale.

- `migration-workaround-rollback-and-user-notification`: migration workaround rollback and user
  notification.

- `tests-artifact-digests-expiry-review-and-retrospective`: tests artifact digests expiry review and
  retrospective.

The exception can shorten notice; it cannot avoid the SemVer impact, migration evidence, immutable
artifact, user communication, or rollback requirement. It can never waive:

- `repository-root-filesystem-boundary`: repository root filesystem boundary.

- `normal-scan-no-command-execution-no-network-and-read-only-default`: normal scan no command
  execution no network and read only default.

- `signature-digest-schema-channel-and-engine-verification`: signature digest schema channel and
  engine verification.

- `secret-redaction-and-no-external-repository-mutation`: secret redaction and no external
  repository mutation.

- `atomic-range-bounded-concurrent-change-safe-fixes`: atomic range bounded concurrent change safe
  fixes.

- `immutable-versioned-artifacts-and-audit-record`: immutable versioned artifacts and audit record.

## Primary standards basis

Reviewed 2026-08-02:

- [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/) defines the public API, immutable released
  versions, patch/minor/major meanings, and a minor release for deprecation before later major
  removal.
- [JSON Schema: declaring a schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/basics)
  recommends an explicit dialect `$schema` and unique `$id`.
- [npm's Unpublish Policy](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish/) explains that registry data
  is immutable, an unpublished name/version cannot be reused, and deprecation preserves availability
  for dependent builds. The
  [npm deprecation guidance](https://docs.npmjs.com/deprecating-and-undeprecating-packages-or-package-versions/)
  recommends deprecation instead of unpublishing.
- [The Update Framework 1.0.35 specification](https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/v1.0.35/)
  defines threshold trust and defenses against rollback, freeze, mix-and-match, and wrong-target
  attacks. H02 owns the exact implementation profile and any later TUF-version adoption; this policy
  does not silently select one.
